chunks: By this chain of transmission, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from Abu Basir, who said:

I visited Umm Humayda to console her over [the death of] Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). She wept, and I wept due to her weeping. Then she said: O Abu Muhammad! If you had seen Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at the time of his death, you would have witnessed something astonishing,

He opened his eyes and said: 'Gather for me all those who have kinship with me.' She said: We did not leave a single person out — all were gathered. She said: Then he looked at them and said: 'Surely, our intercession does not reach one who takes prayer lightly.'

key_terms.شفاعتنا: Our intercession — referring to the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt (the Prophet's household and the Imams) on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.قرابة: Kinship, blood relation — the Imam gathered all relatives as witnesses to his final teaching
key_terms.مستخفًّا بالصلاة: One who takes prayer lightly — i.e., one who neglects, belittles, or is heedless toward the obligatory salat

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about intercession and prayer at his deathbed?
ai.summary: This hadith preserves a moving account from Abu Basir's visit to Umm Humayda — the wife of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) — shortly after the Imam's death. She recounts the Imam's final act: gathering all his relatives to witness his last declaration. The dying Imam's solemn warning that the Ahl al-Bayt's intercession on the Day of Judgment does not extend to those who treat salat with contempt reflects the central importance of prayer in Shia piety, understood as the pillar of religion.
